title: Introduce ephemeral KMS credentials and scopeable RBAC profiles for region-restricted workloads
author: Asha Patel
description:
Motivation: customers operating in export-controlled and regulated jurisdictions have requested stronger operational guarantees that keys and audit records cannot be used outside explicit regions. This PR introduces two complementary controls: (1) ephemeral per-request KMS credentials minted only for the target region and scoped to the service principal, and (2) RBAC v2 'scopeable profiles' which allow operators to attach region and data-class constraints to roles and grants. The goal is to make region pinning enforceable end-to-end (gateway -> router -> serving runtime) and to cryptographically bind audit events to the region-limited KMS envelope.

What this change introduces (high level):
- Ephemeral KMS broker in auth-service that mints short-lived, region-bound credentials with constrained CMK usage (sign/decrypt only for approved contexts).
- RBAC v2 profile objects (rbac_profile.yaml) that embed attributes: allowed_regions, allowed_data_classes, max_ttl_seconds. Profiles are referenced by RoleBindings.
- Gateway checks to reject requests when request principal's active profile does not include the requested region or data class.
- Audit annotator that signs each audit envelope with the ephemeral credential and emits a region-proof header (X-RW-Region-Proof) consumed by ingestion pipeline.
- Fallback policy for operator workflows: a new 'override-with-justification' flow that records a signed escalation claim when human operators need to perform cross-region actions.

Implementation notes: all code changes are behind a feature flag (rbac_v2_scopes_ephemeral_kms). The PR includes: auth-service (broker and minting logic), gateway (pre-authorization filter), policy-evaluator (profile resolution and decision cache), audit-writer (signed-envelope writer), and integration tests + a CLI tool for generating test proofs.

Files changed (high-level):
- auth-service/src/broker/ephemeral_kms.go (new)
- policy/evaluator/profile.go (new)
- gateway/middleware/region_check.go (new)
- audit/writer/signed_envelope.go (new)
- proto/rbac/v2/profile.proto (new)
- deploy/helm/values.featureflags.yaml (feature flag)
- docs/security/ephemeral-kms-and-profiles.md (new docs and operator runbook)
- ci/integration/ephemeral-kms-test.sh (integration harness)
- tests/integration/region_profile_e2e_test.go (new test)

Testing and verification:
- Unit tests added for profile evaluation and expiry semantics.
- Integration tests simulate a cross-region request and assert that the gateway rejects without escalation; then run the override flow and assert audit envelope contains X-RW-Region-Proof signed by region-limited key.
- Manual QA with staging KMS provider (mock) verified signed envelopes are verifiable by audit indexer.

Backwards compatibility and rollout plan:
- Feature gated: default off.
- Phased rollout: enable for a small cohort (internal customers) and run audit-only mode where gateway logs violations without rejecting. After 2 weeks of low violations, enable enforcement.
- Migration: existing RoleBindings without explicit profile reference will implicitly use legacy 'global' profile until operator migrates. A migration helper script is included in deploy/ops/migrate-rolebindings.sh.

Security review notes:
- Key usage is intentionally constrained; ephemeral creds cannot be exported and KMS ACLs prevent cross-region unwrap operations.
- Audit envelopes include the ephemeral key fingerprint to make non-repudiation practical.
- New code paths were fuzz-tested and code-scanned (Snyk/GitHub CodeQL) with no critical findings.

Release notes: "Add optional ephemeral KMS credentials and RBAC v2 scopeable profiles to allow region-locked operations and signed audit envelopes (feature-flagged)."

Checklist: [x] design doc linked (Linear ENG-3021) [x] tests added [x] docs and runbook [x] security scan [x] migration helper script

Rollout/rollback: the feature flag allows safe rollback. If there are key provisioning issues, operators can flip to audit-only mode while we remediate.

review_comments: Benji Romero: This looks comprehensive. A couple questions: how do we handle clock skew for TTL checks? -> Author: we add a 30s skew tolerance and log when skew exceeds threshold. See profile.go:line 112 for tolerance code.
Clara Nguyen: Can the feature flag be toggled without restart? -> Author: yes, feature flags are read from the config service; we added a watcher to hot-reload without process restart.

Diego Silva: Concern about increased latency on cold key mint. Did you add caching? -> Author: ephemeral credentials are cached per-priority-window (100ms) and minting is async for warm paths; see auth-service broker cache implementation.
